articles.title: Auditing Political Alignment in LLM Assistants: Engagement, Stance, and User Identity
articles.summary: The paper audits political behavior across six LLM systems and argues that AI assistants operate under distinct “speech regimes” that vary by topic, user identity, engagement, and stance. In a preregistered experiment of 7,500 multi-turn conversations, systems showed different patterns of refusal, accommodation, and firmness across topics such as abortion, climate change, Nazism, Catalan independence, and a control topic.
articles.advisor_relevance: This matters because political alignment, refusal behavior, and user-specific accommodation are emerging governance risks for widely deployed AI assistants.
